summary: Range towers on Race Point and Virago Point, lit 15 Nov 1902 to guide ships through Porlier Pass; de-staffed 1996 after the front tower was replaced.

structures.type: square wooden tower with octagonal lantern
square wooden tower, sloping sides, square lantern

access.note: The land belongs to the Penelakut Tribe; Lighthouse Friends advises getting permission before crossing it.

events.note: Fairway buoy established off the east entrance to Porlier Pass (November 1901)
Front and rear range lights put in operation 15 November 1902
Four-roomed keeper's cottage built by contract ($725); cistern added by day labour
Paddle steamer Del Norte lost near Canoe Reef after entering the pass in fog (10 or 11 Nov, sources differ)
Canadian Pacific Railway transfer barge ashore at Porlier Pass, second half of December 1921
Steel tug Point Grey struck Virago Rock, 26 Feb 1949
Race Point front tower removed (Feb 1996) and replaced by a cylindrical fibreglass tower
Station de-staffed two months after the tower change

notes_for_editor: 1) Keeper appointment dates: the 1909 keepers' table (scan p.180, printed p.173) was checked on the page image: the Portier Pass row carries F. Allison and Nov. 15, 1902 on one line. The 1905 and 1906 tables print 'Nov. 12, 1902' for the same station (OCR), against 'Nov. 15, 1902' in 1909; the story uses 15 November, which matches the lighting date in the 1902 report. 2) Lighthouse Friends' keeper list names Peter Sit-who-latza for 1902, but its narrative says the marine agent's plan to hire him was overruled. No Marine table in the local corpus names him. He stays in the roster with that note. 3) Allison's first name: Lighthouse Friends gives Francis Togan Allison; the Marine tables print Frank Fagan Allison (1903) and F. F. Allison (fiscal 1911-12). The story uses the Marine form and gives both. 4) Keepers after 1960 (Noble to Ray) are named only as Lighthouse Friends lists them, with no personal detail. 5) Lighthouse Friends reports a violent quarrel in 1929. It is a single community-site account of a private dispute with no primary source, so the story leaves it out and says only that the couple separated and the marine agent nearly dismissed him. 6) The 1902 report describes fixed white lights; the Coast Guard list now gives F Y (yellow). The sources do not date the change. The 1902 range is 'visible 9 miles in the line of range'; the list gives a nominal range of 10 nautical miles. 7) Del Norte: UASBC gives 10 Nov 1868 and a 10 m depth; CoastView gives 11 Nov and over ten fathoms (about 18 m); captain spelled Windsor and Winsor. Both are secondary. The story now gives UASBC's account without its garbled reef name. The 1868 loss is not in the local corpus (which starts in 1900). 8) The Point Grey date (26 Feb 1949) comes from CoastView only; the heritage register was checked for location and depth. 9) The December 1921 barge: the salvage list prints 'December IS to 30' (OCR), read as 15 to 30 December; the year is 1921 from the list's heading groups. The barge's name is garbled in OCR ('Vo. S') and is left out. 10) Rear tower height (31 ft), lens types and the Virago Point location come from Lighthouse Friends only (the Coast Guard list gives coordinates, not the name); the Sit-who-latza, petition and Christmas-pudding anecdotes are attributed in the story. The octagonal lantern is in Lighthouse Friends and CoastView; no 1902 OCR hit was found for it. 11) Lighthouse Friends and CoastView are copyrighted or community sources; the story paraphrases them and quotes at most a few words. 12) The Marine reports in the local corpus start in 1900; no Porlier-specific report before 1901 was available. 13) Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 1908 tide-table sentence now names both passes; the 1996 de-staffing is footnoted to the sources that give it; the 1912 list is called fiscal 1911-12; the Coast Guard list is cited only for what it gives (F Y, focal height, range, 24 h).
